sections.h2: City or county: check this first
sections.html:
Albemarle County wraps around Charlottesville on every side, yet the city stands alone as its own government while serving as the county seat. Population was 46,553 in 2020 and is put at 44,388 for 2025. Count Albemarle, Fluvanna, Greene and Nelson counties together and the metro area holds about 221,524 people.

Pin down your parcel's jurisdiction early. A Charlottesville mailing address can belong to a house in Albemarle County, and then the tax office, permit desk and zoning code are the county's. Even most of the university grounds fall under the county. Whoever sends your tax bill is the office to phone about anything owed.

Settlement began in 1762 along a trade route that follows today's U.S. 250, and rail came later. Court Square marks the original center, with the Downtown Mall next to it. Repair needs split by age. A home near that old core often has aging wiring, pipes and roofing, whereas a house in a later subdivision raises other questions about mechanical systems and warranties.

Our first question to any owner is the build year, since it decides what we look for on a walkthrough. Dig out permits and receipts for earlier work too. They show a buyer what was already fixed and can firm up an offer.

The University of Virginia and its health system anchor local jobs, with city government, the schools and some research and finance employers behind them. During the academic year over 20,000 students arrive, and rentals near campus feel it. Only about 18 percent of people working in the city also live there. The other 82 percent commute in, and 42 percent of them come from Albemarle County. Another 11,497 residents commute out.

So a seller inside the city is bidding for the same buyers as county sellers. University of Virginia Hospital and Martha Jefferson Hospital both employ and house staff nearby, and Piedmont Virginia Community College draws more renters.

sections.h2: Weather and what to check on the house
sections.html:
Expect humid heat in summer, cool winters and some rain every month. Highs top 90 degrees on roughly 34 days a year. Snow adds up to 17 inches in an average season but melts fast. May through September is wettest, which is hard on gutters, attics and cooling equipment.

  • Run the air conditioner and save the latest service slip.
  • Climb into the attic and look over the roof surface.
  • After a storm, watch for pooling or washout near the foundation.
  • Crawl spaces hold moisture, so look there too.

On the state disclosure form the owner makes no statement about flood hazard areas, dam break inundation zones, radon zones or marine clay soils, so buyers dig into those themselves. Mentioning a past water problem up front earns goodwill.

Drivers rely on Interstate 64 and U.S. 29, plus U.S. 250 and Virginia Route 20. Charlottesville Area Transit covers city bus routes, JAUNT runs paratransit vans, and University Transit Service loops the campus area. Flights leave from Charlottesville-Albemarle Airport. Amtrak stops three days a week for the Cardinal, and the Crescent and Northeast Regional run daily.

Walkable streets near the Downtown Mall or a bus line attract renters and downsizers, while houses farther out suit drivers. Our cash offers reflect whichever group the property fits.

City schools consist of six elementary schools, Walker Upper Elementary School, Buford Middle School and Charlottesville High School. Albemarle County Public Schools handle the rest of the area. The district can hint at which jurisdiction you are in, because some private schools with Charlottesville postal addresses actually sit in the county. Before listing, renting or renovating, phone the city's planning and building offices and the treasurer to confirm local requirements.

sections.h2: What Virginia sellers pay and sign
sections.html:
The seller owes a grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 of the price unless the contract moves it. State and locality split the proceeds, and the circuit court clerk holds back recording until it is paid. See Virginia Code 58.1-802.

Every seller must deliver the Real Estate Board's residential property disclosure statement. Among the topics where the owner makes no representations are historic district rules, lot lines, adjacent parcels, flood hazards, easements, lead plumbing, drywall and any dam. From January 1, 2027, the statute adds an item on use-value assessment and roll-back taxes. Read Virginia Code 55.1-703.

A real estate tax bill left unpaid becomes a lien ranking above the others, and at closing the agent takes it out of your proceeds. Who covers which days of the current year is a matter for the contract. The lien rule is in Virginia Code 58.1-3340.

  • Request a payoff amount from the treasurer ahead of closing.
  • Let the title company hunt for liens and judgments.
  • Put in writing who covers the grantor's tax and recording fees.

sections.h2: Paperwork to gather before you call anyone
sections.html:
A little preparation shortens the whole process. Pull together your latest tax bill, the deed, and any permits or receipts for roof, heating or plumbing work. If the house sits near the city and county line, note which jurisdiction mails your bill, since that decides which treasurer, planning office and permit desk you deal with.

Then walk the house with the disclosure form in hand. Topics like flood hazard, easements and lead plumbing are ones where you make no representation, but a buyer will still ask, so know what you can say about water in the crawl space, the age of the roof and the condition of the cooling system. Heirs selling an inherited house should also line up whoever has authority to sign the deed, because the title company will want to see that before it schedules a closing.

With no mortgage involved, a cash deal avoids lender delays, appraisal problems and loan approvals. The path looks like this:

  1. Send us the address and a few details.
  2. We look the property over and put an offer in writing.
  3. Once you agree, a title company prepares the deed, payoffs and closing papers.
  4. You choose the closing day that suits your move.

City owners often come to us with an inherited house, a rental in rough shape, or a place they must leave fast for a new job. Furniture can stay and repairs can wait, because we take the property as it stands. An offer you decline costs you nothing, and an agent listing remains open to you.

This page is general background on Charlottesville and not legal or tax advice. An attorney or the local government can confirm the details for your case.

faqs.a: No. The city is the county seat but governs itself separately. Look at your tax bill to see which one covers your parcel.

faqs.q: How many people live in Charlottesville?
faqs.a: The 2020 census found 46,553 residents, and 44,388 is the 2025 estimate.

faqs.q: What does Virginia charge a seller when a deed is recorded?
faqs.a: Code 58.1-802 puts a grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 of the price on the seller, though the contract may hand part or all of it to the buyer. The clerk takes payment at recording.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Charlottesville without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. The state form leaves due diligence to the buyer, so an as-is sale is fine. You still owe the buyer the Real Estate Board's disclosure statement.

faqs.q: Which airport and train station serve Charlottesville?
faqs.a: Commercial flights use Charlottesville-Albemarle Airport. Amtrak's Cardinal, Crescent and some Northeast Regional trains stop at the station.
